visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Harbour sells for £1,300m with £375m of debt left, after repaying £225m from its own cash. What does the fund get?
questions.explain: Exit value minus the debt still owed: 1,300 − 375 = 925. The 225 of cash already went into repaying debt, so adding it again, as Sofia did, counts it twice.
questions.explain_at: Count it once, in the debt

questions.q: Over five years Harbour has £590m of EBITDA, £50m of depreciation and £240m of interest, taxed at 25%. How much tax does it pay?
questions.explain: Tax is on profit after depreciation and interest: 25% × (590 − 50 − 240) = 75. Taxing the whole EBITDA, Sofia's slip, gives about 150.
questions.explain_at: Tax is charged on profit, not on EBITDA

questions.q: A fund turns £400m into £925m in five years. Roughly what is the IRR?
questions.explain: 2.3x sits between doubling in five years (about 15%) and 2.5x (about 20%). Dividing the 131% gain by five gives 26%, which forgets compounding.
questions.explain_at: Two point three sits in between, nearer the top

questions.q: A fund needs a 20% IRR and expects £925m of equity at exit in five years. Roughly how much equity can it put in today?
questions.explain: 20% a year compounds to about 2.5x over five years, so 925 ÷ 2.5 ≈ 370. Halving it, as Sofia did, treats the return as simple interest.
questions.explain_at: Twenty percent a year for five years is about two and a half times

questions.q: Ahold Delhaize quotes about 7.2x EBITDA for Tesco's Czech and Slovak businesses, and 5.0x. What's the difference?
questions.explain: Both are on the lease-adjusted basis; 5.0x adds the synergies Ahold Delhaize expects from combining Tesco with its Albert chain to the EBITDA.
questions.explain_at: Five point zero times including synergies
